description:
## Highlights
- **Songs no longer stop about 30 seconds in.** On phones where YouTube's token can't be made, the song now comes from a source that needs none and plays to the end, and a stream refused mid-song carries on from the same second ([#23](https://github.com/rajendra7169/blazify/issues/23))
- **Half the download:** about 14 MB instead of 29 MB. The Japanese reading dictionary is fetched only when you ask for Japanese lyrics in English letters, and Home's pictures are smaller files
- **Music keeps going without a connection:** on Wi-Fi the next three songs are saved to the phone, and with no connection the queue goes on with songs that are there instead of stopping
- **Offline, Home plays what you have:** the shuffle button, For you and Speed dial play the songs saved on your phone, shuffled, instead of an online radio that fails
- **Sync a song's plain lyrics yourself:** tap along as it plays and the lines light up in time from then on

## New features
- Remove from queue in a song's menu, not only by swiping it away
- Discord shows Blazify as what you are listening on
- The Ring player has shuffle on the left and repeat on the right, with the standard play button, so the controls stay put when the lyrics open
- Spanish has every newer text, for Spain and Latin America, and the last English words in screens follow the app's language

## Fixes and improvements
- **The search screen no longer breaks after you delete a search:** Recent searches and Browse show cleanly instead of over the old results ([#24](https://github.com/rajendra7169/blazify/issues/24))
- A song YouTube turns away with a "confirm you're not a bot" check is asked for again with a fresh session, instead of being skipped as unavailable
- Going back while editing a search returns to its results with the words they belong to
- Last.fm scrobbling works again (in the F-Droid build, add your own Last.fm key)
- Shuffle with crossfade keeps one shuffled order instead of repeating songs and skipping others
- With explicit songs or videos hidden, tapping a song in a list plays that song, not the one that moved into its place
- A playlist sorted by artist keeps each artist's songs together, ordered by album
- Lyrics: outside full screen the current line sits a little lower, so the line just sung no longer hides behind the Sources button
- Equalizer graph: negative dB labels keep their minus sign, and the 100, 1k and 10k labels are no longer cut in half
- The playback error report shows the real time of the error
- Release builds no longer include a design-preview screen that other apps could open

---

**Also on this page:** `Blazify.apk` for phones without Google services, and `Blazify-izzy-9.18.0.apk`,
the build with no updater for F-Droid-style repositories.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/rajendra7169/blazify/compare/v9.17.0...v9.18.0

## Highlights
- **Opens about twice as fast** — Home appears in roughly half the time it used to, straight from the launch screen, on every phone
- **A new look for loading** — Blazify's own logo tells its little story wherever the app waits. No separate splash screen any more
- **Browse, mood and genre pages, redone** — the moods, then Genres under their own heading, ordered by what you listen to; mood pages open whole with big cards and songs as a list, with a placeholder in the right shape while they load
- **Smoother on every phone** — Search scrolls smoothly again, Home's shelves are reused as they scroll, and the screen rests when nothing is changing
- **Updates keep coming even if GitHub doesn't answer** — the app falls back to Blazify's own website, downloads from GitLab and then Codeberg, and picks up a dropped download where it stopped

## New features
- **One button row for playlists and albums** — like and download on the left, Play in the middle, shuffle and more on the right; a playlist from Browse downloads in one tap
- Lists open on the song that is playing, instead of a Jump to playing button
- Download sits among the first tiles of a song's menu
- Every cover shows the Blazify mark while it loads, or when a song has none
- Home's greeting card takes the colour of the song that is playing
- Blaze Together runs on Blazify's own server, and says why if a room can't be made

## Fixes and improvements
- **Quick picks, Daily discover and radio find related songs again** — YouTube had moved them, and Quick picks fell to a single song
- Forgotten favourites holds the songs you have stopped playing, not only the ones you still play
- Choosing another song after one failed to load now plays it, instead of staying on the error
- A song link that opens Blazify always plays, even when it arrives before the player is ready
- Fixed a crash when a cover could not load, for example with no connection
- Pressing Next shows the new cover at once instead of a placeholder
- Quick picks stay where they first appear instead of reshuffling a few seconds after Home opens
- Video Art plays through a song's last 45 seconds instead of freezing, picks the official video closest in length to the song, and goes round again when the video is shorter
- Better Lyrics signs in when a song plays, not when the app opens
- Onboarding stays inside the screen edges, so Skip can always be pressed
- A finished update download is kept even when its name is already taken in Downloads

---

**Also on this page:** `Blazify.apk` for phones without Google services, and `Blazify-izzy-9.17.0.apk`,
the build with no updater for F-Droid-style repositories.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/rajendra7169/blazify/compare/v9.16.0...v9.17.0

## Highlights
- **Video Art player** — the song's own official video plays behind the player, muted and in step with the audio. It stays off on mobile data unless you ask for it
- **Import a playlist from Spotify** — paste a share link and Blazify rebuilds it, song by song
- **Skip the talking** — SponsorBlock skips intros, outros and non-music sections, and the lyrics shift with it so the words still match
- **Radio stations play** — the live broadcasts in Listen together now work, marked LIVE while they are on air
- **Block an artist** and they stay out of Home, search, picks and radio
- Sideways works: every player design, the theme gallery and Look & Feel are laid out for a phone on its side
- The app is now translated into 15 more languages

## New features
- **Swipe a song in the queue to the right** to play it next — no dragging it up eighty places
- **Share a playlist** as a link or a QR code; opening one offers to keep it
- **Jump to the playing song** in a long playlist, album or library list
- **Play this a few times** — repeat a song 2, 3, 5 or 10 times, then carry on
- **ListenBrainz** scrobbling, beside Last.fm
- Speed dial and For you play straight from the greeting card on Home
- Updates download inside the app now, with a progress bar, instead of handing the file to a browser
- The queue got a proper look: one-line header, rounded artwork, amber shuffle and repeat, and it fades into the bar at the foot
- Lyrics: the pill at the top is called **Sources**, because that is what it opens — the same words from every provider, so you can take whichever is best in time. It steps out of the way in full screen
- Settings shows who is signed in, with your channel picture

## Fixes and improvements
- **Keep playing through a connection drop** — minutes of the song are fetched ahead, and a lost connection is picked up when it returns
- Search shows results as soon as YouTube answers instead of waiting for artist lookups — about three times quicker
- A song is put on top of the results when YouTube leads with a video of it
- Artist names are read properly: no more songs by "4:41", "2026" or ","
- Downloads that did not finish are asked for again at startup, and a failed one says so
- Songs on your phone play straight off the phone, with their own covers kept
- A song that loads but never starts is skipped instead of buffering for ever
- The play button takes its colour from the artwork on every design, and the duplicate cast button is gone from the album art
- The sleep timer opens as a sheet like the keys beside it, not a box in the middle of the screen
- Fixed a crash that could kill the app at launch after the sideways work

---

**Also on this page:** `Blazify.apk` for phones without Google services, and `Blazify-izzy-9.16.0.apk`,
the build with no updater for F-Droid-style repositories.

## Highlights
- Songs no longer waste their first attempt on YouTube's web player before starting
- **Don't play this song** keeps a song out of queues, radio, recommendations and Android Auto
- Double-tap to seek on every player design, as far as you choose (5, 10, 15 or 30 seconds)
- Lyrics stay in sync better, with new settings for text size, line spacing, glow and animation style
- Podcasts remember their own playback speed

## New features
- **Get beta updates** switch in Settings › Updater, to try new versions early
- Play/pause tile for Quick Settings, and Liked, Downloads and Shuffle app shortcuts
- Mobile data controls: save data on mobile networks, download only on Wi-Fi
- Charts and New release albums in the Search tab
- Choose whether new songs go to the top or the bottom of a playlist
- **Copy details** button on the playback error card
- Report a problem opens a short bug report form with your version and phone filled in
- Universal x86 and x86_64 support (Waydroid, emulators, x86 tablets and TV boxes)

## Fixes and improvements
- A stream that has expired gets a fresh link, and a song that loads but never plays is skipped
- Opening a song link plays it straight away instead of loading the old queue first
- Playback position is saved every few seconds, and shuffle stays on after closing the app
- Back on the lyrics screen returns to the player instead of closing it
- Play next picks play in the order you pick them, and swipe to queue is on by default
- Charts show chart playlists and top artists instead of an empty page
- Wrapped appears every December and January, for the right year
- "Age-restricted" only shows when the error really says so
- Downloads use full quality on Auto, and expired download links are fetched again
- Cassette player: named bottom keys, placed lower with even spacing
- Removed unused settings and the Appearance options that repeated Look & Feel

## Downloads
- **Blazify-gms.apk**: for almost everybody, casting included
- **Blazify.apk**: for a phone with no Google services, or if you would rather keep them out of it. No casting
- **Blazify-izzy-9.14.0.apk**: the F-Droid build with in-app updates switched off, please don't download it
- Signing key SHA-256: `9e:25:8a:a0:0a:d2:29:1b:67:b8:1f:69:5a:f0:65:dc:72:6f:99:e0:df:31:d0:44:d3:a6:1d:06:33:84:3e:45`

<summary>SHA-256 checksums</summary>

```

4e4ce94f49538c42e223c76e56a6593f2869485c199bc58f92807becbfa1e6fd  Blazify-gms-9.14.0.apk
```

</details>

**Coming from 9.12.3 or earlier?** Those were signed with an older key: back up your library, uninstall, then install this one. [Steps](https://github.com/rajendra7169/blazify/blob/main/MIGRATION.md)

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/rajendra7169/blazify/compare/v9.13.3...v9.14.0

**If you are on 9.13.2, update.** On some phones it closed itself as it opened,
before you could touch anything.

## The crash

The catalogue does not always say how long an audio file is. Blazify insisted
that it had, and when it had not, it threw on a background thread where nothing
was watching. The whole app went down rather than losing one song's
volume-levelling figures.

It did not happen on every phone, because it depends which track you land on.
Where it did happen it was unusable: closing on launch, and again when a song
started.

Reported through Settings, About, Report a problem from a realme phone on
Android 13. That report is the only reason it was found. Thank you.

## Why it could happen at all

That work runs on a background thread, and the code around it had already
returned by the time it ran, so it could catch nothing. Nothing else was
catching anything either. Sixty-four pieces of background work in the player ran
that way, and five of them said what to do if they failed.

None of it is worth closing a music player for: a scrobble that does not send, a
cover that will not load, a queue that cannot be saved. All of it is survivable
now. A failure is written to the log and playing carries on.

## Release notes you can read

Notes are written for this page, where GitHub draws headings and tables. Inside
the app they were arriving with their own punctuation: pipes, backticks, and
sentences broken wherever the line had been wrapped. They read as prose now, and
the changelog is signed with the app's own mark rather than a stray progress bar.

## Also

The developer photo is the current one.

## The other two files

Most people want the link at the top. The other two are:

Blazify-gms-9.13.3.apk, only if you cast to a speaker or a TV.

Blazify-izzy-9.13.3.apk, which you should not download. It is the F-Droid build,
published so F-Droid can verify it, and in-app updates are switched off in it.

## From 9.13.2, if you skipped it

Local files play again, the first song starts in about three seconds instead of
ten or more, you can correct a badly named file's title and artist, browse your
own music by folder, and leave out short recordings like voice notes.

The other two files, and why you probably don't want them
| file | who it is for | |---|---| | **`Blazify.apk`** | **You** — the button above. Works everywhere, updates itself | | `Blazify-gms-9.13.2.apk` | Only if you cast to a speaker or a TV | | `Blazify-izzy-9.13.2.apk` | **Don't download this one.** It is the F-Droid build, published so F-Droid can verify it. In-app updates are switched off, so it will never tell you about a new version |
--- If you are on 9.13.0, take this one. Two things that version promised did not work at all, and both are fixed here. ## The first song starts It was taking ten seconds or more, and on a slower phone it often never started at all. Every launch was working out from scratch that the site's current player cannot be read here, which costs megabytes of parsing before anything can play, and it threw that answer away when you closed the app. It now writes the answer down and picks it up again next time. The token the first request needs was also being warmed too late to be any help. It arrived after the song had already asked for one, then competed with it. Measured on a 2019 phone: **around three seconds, every time.** ## Music on your phone actually plays 9.13.0 added local files and none of them could play. The player had been given only the two formats the online catalogue uses, so MP3, FLAC, Ogg, Opus and WAV had nothing to read them with and stopped the moment they were asked to start. Cover art shows up where it was blank. A song whose file never named an artist is given one. Formats the player genuinely cannot open are no longer listed at all rather than listed and then refused. ## Telling a file what it is Music that arrives on a phone is named by whatever put it there, so a song can sit in your library as `AUD-20260905-WA0014` with no artist and no way to say otherwise. Now there is: **⋮ → Edit** on any local song sets its title, artist and album, and the correction survives a rescan. Clearing the boxes puts the file's own tags back. Corrections are kept inside Blazify. The file itself is left alone, so other apps still see its original tags. ## Folders, and leaving things out Local music can be browsed the way it is actually arranged: **Music on this device → the folder icon**. **Settings → Storage** can now leave out the shortest and smallest files, so a seventeen second voice note from a chat stops sitting next to your albums. Both start at no limit. ## Everything else - Room invites go to a page that exists. The old address was never registered - The profile icon opens the account sheet instead of jumping past it to the login page, and that sheet checks for a new version where it stands - Menus no longer offer a local file things it cannot do: no radio built from it, no link to copy that opens nothing, no album page, no blank details sheet - Home leaves no gap under a short shelf, the last row of a list sits clear of the mini player, and pulling to refresh brings different songs rather than the same ones rearranged
